# Get started contributing to tiny-sum

This guide takes you from a fresh copy of the repository to a passing test
run, so you know your setup works before you change any code. It takes about
five minutes.

tiny-sum is a small JavaScript library that adds numbers and rejects anything
that is not a number. For a one-line summary, see the [project README](../README.md).

## Contents

- [Check the prerequisites](#check-the-prerequisites)
- [Run the tests](#run-the-tests)
- [Find your way around the code](#find-your-way-around-the-code)
- [Make and test a change](#make-and-test-a-change)
- [Run only some tests](#run-only-some-tests)

## Check the prerequisites

You need **Node.js 20 or later**. The `engines` field in `package.json` sets
this minimum. npm comes with Node.js.

1. From any directory, check your Node.js version:

   ```sh
   node --version
   ```

   The output must be `v20.0.0` or higher, for example `v22.13.0`.

2. Check that npm is installed:

   ```sh
   npm --version
   ```

   Any version number, for example `11.20.0`, means npm is ready.

The project has no dependencies, so you do not need to run `npm install`.

## Run the tests

Run this from the repository root, which is the folder that contains
`package.json`:

```sh
npm test
```

This runs `node --test`, the test runner built into Node.js. A working setup
ends with a summary like this:

```text
# tests 2
# suites 0
# pass 2
# fail 0
```

If `# fail` shows a number other than `0`, the lines starting `not ok` name
the failing tests.

## Find your way around the code

| Path | What it holds |
| --- | --- |
| `src/sum.js` | The library. It exports one function, `sum(...values)`. |
| `test/sum.test.js` | Tests, written with `node:test` and `node:assert/strict`. |
| `package.json` | Package name, version, the `test` script, and the Node.js minimum. |

`sum` adds every argument it receives. It throws a `TypeError` with the
message `not a number: <value>` if any argument is not a number or is `NaN`.

## Make and test a change

1. Edit the code in `src/sum.js`.
2. Add or update a test in `test/sum.test.js` that covers your change. Follow
   the existing pattern of one `test(...)` call for each behavior.
3. Run the tests again from the repository root:

   ```sh
   npm test
   ```

   Your change is ready for review when the summary shows `# fail 0`.

The Node.js test runner finds files whose names end in `.test.js`. Put any new
test files in `test/` and give them that ending.

## Run only some tests

To run a single test file:

```sh
node --test test/sum.test.js
```

To run only the tests whose names match a pattern, such as `rejects text`:

```sh
node --test --test-name-pattern="rejects"
```

The summary shows `# tests 1` when only one test matches.
